[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-001-ai-agent-definition.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This standard establishes the mandatory definition format for every enterprise AI agent — AI Agents (Configured) and Custom AI Agents — so that each capability is understandable, governable, and supportable in a federated delivery model. It defines the metadata, capability contract, and required deliverables that every agent must maintain at all lifecycle states.
page_texts.5:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-001-ai-agent-definition.md#scope]

### Scope

This standard applies to all AI Agents (Configured) and Custom AI Agents at all lifecycle states (Proposed, Pilot, Production, Contained, Retired). It does not apply to Automation (RPA and Workflow) or Intelligent Automation capabilities. See [GUID-TEC-AI-001](../../../strategy/guidance/technology/ai/GUID-TEC-AI-001-ai-automation-classification-guidance.md) for capability classification guidance.
page_texts.6:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-001-ai-agent-definition.md#compliance-level]

### Compliance Level

Mandatory. All AI agents must comply with this standard before promotion to Pilot state.
page_texts.7:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-001-ai-agent-definition.md#business-rationale]

### Business Rationale

Without a standardized definition format, AI agents in a federated portfolio become ungovernable: ownership is unclear, capability scope is undefined, and quality expectations are absent. This standard is the foundation for all other AI agent governance standards.

[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-001-ai-agent-definition.md#mandatory-requirements]

### Mandatory Requirements

Every AI agent definition must include all of the following.

**Mandatory Metadata (9 fields):**

- Agent name — following the naming convention in STD-TEC-AI-007 for M365-deployed agents (AI Agents (Configured) and Custom AI Agents deployed through M365 Agent Builder or Copilot Studio); non-M365 custom agents (such as API-integrated custom agents) must follow the naming intent of STD-TEC-AI-007 (provider-role-capability-version structure) but the M365-specific character limits and platform constraints do not apply. Codex-based development is outside this governance framework's scope per STD-TEC-AI-007.
- Capability domain — the business capability domain this agent belongs to
- Business purpose — a single sentence describing the primary business outcome the agent delivers
- Owner role and owner name — the named individual responsible for the agent's capability contract and lifecycle
- Backup owner — a named individual who can assume ownership responsibilities
- Lifecycle state — one of: Proposed, Pilot, Production, Contained, Retired
- Policy classification — the data sensitivity and compliance classification applicable to this agent's evidence sources and outputs
- Last validation date — the date the agent's quality rubric was last evaluated against representative scenarios
- Current version — following the versioning convention in STD-TEC-AI-007

**Mandatory Capability Contract (6 core fields + 1 conditional field):**

- In-scope intents — explicit list of what the agent is designed to handle
- Out-of-scope intents — explicit list of what the agent must not attempt to handle
- Primary user personas — the role tiers and job functions the agent is designed for
- Expected business outcomes — measurable outcomes the agent is expected to deliver
- Handoff or escalation boundaries — conditions under which the agent must transfer the interaction to a human or another system
- Dependencies on other capabilities — other agents, tools, or data sources this agent requires to function
- System connections — a declaration of every external system the agent connects to, including connection classification, identity model, and permitted operations; required for any agent with external connections (see STD-TEC-AI-008)

**Required Deliverables:**

Every agent in Pilot or Production state must maintain:

1. Capability Contract document
2. Intent Catalog
3. Evidence Map (see STD-TEC-AI-002)
4. Output Contract (see STD-TEC-AI-003)
5. Quality Rubric (see STD-TEC-AI-005)
6. Change Log entry (see STD-TEC-AI-004 and STD-GOV-AI-004)
7. System Connection Register (see STD-TEC-AI-008) — required for any agent with one or more external system connections
page_texts.10:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-001-ai-agent-definition.md#recommended-practices]

### Recommended Practices

- Review the capability contract quarterly to confirm it accurately reflects the agent's current scope
- Align the business purpose statement with the capability domain vocabulary to support portfolio discoverability
- Document escalation boundaries with enough specificity to allow a user to recognize when an escalation condition has been reached
page_texts.11:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-001-ai-agent-definition.md#prohibited-practices]

### Prohibited Practices

- Agents must not be promoted to Pilot or Production without all mandatory metadata fields completed
- Business purpose must not be written as a list — it must be a single sentence to enforce scope clarity
- In-scope and out-of-scope intent lists must not overlap
page_texts.12:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-001-ai-agent-definition.md#exceptions-process]

### Exceptions Process

1. Exceptions to any requirement in this standard require written approval from the Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board
2. Exception requests must include the specific requirement being excepted, the business justification, the risk assessment, and a remediation timeline
3. Approved exceptions are recorded in the capability registry with an expiry date

page_texts.15:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-001-ai-agent-definition.md#metadata-currency]

#### Metadata Currency

- All mandatory metadata fields must remain current at all times; stale metadata is treated as non-compliance
- The last validation date field must be updated whenever the agent's quality rubric is evaluated, regardless of pass or fail outcome
- The current version field must be updated for every behavioral or contract change per STD-TEC-AI-007
page_texts.16:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-001-ai-agent-definition.md#capability-contract-integrity]

#### Capability Contract Integrity

- In-scope and out-of-scope intent lists must be mutually exclusive; any overlap is a contract defect
- Out-of-scope intents must be specific enough to distinguish from in-scope intents — generic exclusions such as "anything not related to this domain" do not satisfy the requirement
- Escalation boundaries must define the conditions, not just state that escalation is possible
page_texts.17:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-001-ai-agent-definition.md#required-deliverables-completeness]

#### Required Deliverables Completeness

- All required deliverables must be present and linked in the capability registry entry before Pilot promotion; agents with external connections must include the System Connection Register
- Deliverables that are placeholders or stubs without substantive content do not satisfy the requirement
page_texts.18:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-001-ai-agent-definition.md#architecture-constraints]

### Architecture Constraints

- Each agent must have one and only one capability domain assignment in the capability registry; cross-domain agents require architecture board approval
- The capability contract must be authored before prompt development begins (see PTN-TEC-AI-009: Contract-First Agent Pattern)

page_texts.21:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-001-ai-agent-definition.md#phase-1-capability-contract-authoring-before-pilot]

#### Phase 1: Capability Contract Authoring (Before Pilot)

1. Draft the mandatory metadata using the capability contract template
2. Define in-scope and out-of-scope intents with the primary user personas as the reference audience
3. Identify and document dependencies on other capabilities and evidence sources
4. Submit for High-Tech governance review using the intake checklist (see GUID-TEC-AI-002)
page_texts.22:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-001-ai-agent-definition.md#phase-2-deliverable-completion-before-pilot-promotion]

#### Phase 2: Deliverable Completion (Before Pilot Promotion)

1. Complete the Evidence Map per STD-TEC-AI-002
2. Complete the Output Contract per STD-TEC-AI-003
3. Complete the Quality Rubric per STD-TEC-AI-005
4. Complete the System Connection Register per STD-TEC-AI-008 for any agent with one or more external system connections; document the business justification for any Service Identity connections
5. Create the initial Change Log entry per STD-TEC-AI-004 and STD-GOV-AI-004
6. Record all deliverables in the capability registry
page_texts.23:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-001-ai-agent-definition.md#phase-3-ongoing-maintenance]

#### Phase 3: Ongoing Maintenance

1. Update the last validation date after each quality rubric evaluation
2. Increment the current version field for any behavioral or contract change
3. Review and update the capability contract at the quarterly review cadence
page_texts.24:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-001-ai-agent-definition.md#validation-criteria]

### Validation Criteria

| Validation Area | Criteria | Verification Method | Evidence Required |
| --------------- | --------- | ------------------- | -------------------- |
| Metadata completeness | All 9 mandatory metadata fields present and non-empty | Registry audit | Capability registry record |
| Contract integrity | In-scope and out-of-scope are non-overlapping and specific | Manual review during governance gate | Capability contract document |
| Business outcome measurability | Business purpose is a single sentence with an observable outcome | Governance review | Capability contract document |
| Ownership assignment | Active owner and backup owner are named individuals with confirmed availability | Owner confirmation | Owner acknowledgment record |
| Deliverables presence | All required deliverables linked in registry; System Connection Register present for agents with external connections | Registry audit | Linked deliverable documents |
page_texts.25:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-001-ai-agent-definition.md#documentation-requirements]

### Documentation Requirements

- Capability Contract document: maintained by the agent owner, reviewed by High-Tech at each lifecycle promotion
- Intent Catalog: a structured list of all in-scope intents with examples; maintained alongside the capability contract
- Change Log: appended to after each behavior, schema, or contract change; linked from the capability registry

---
page_texts.28:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-001-ai-agent-definition.md#assessment-criteria]

#### Assessment Criteria

- Mandatory metadata completeness: all 9 fields present, current, and non-empty in the capability registry
- Capability contract integrity: in-scope and out-of-scope are mutually exclusive; business purpose is a single measurable sentence; escalation boundaries are specific
- Required deliverables: all 7 deliverables present (6 core + System Connection Register for agents with external connections) and substantive (not stubs)
page_texts.29:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-001-ai-agent-definition.md#assessment-process]

#### Assessment Process

1. Monthly: Platform Governance Team performs metadata currency checks across all Production capabilities
2. Quarterly: High-Tech governance review includes contract relevance check
3. Event-driven: after any policy or scope change, the owner must update the affected contract fields and notify the Platform Governance Team
page_texts.30:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-001-ai-agent-definition.md#non-compliance-handling]

### Non-Compliance Handling

- Missing mandatory metadata: block promotion to Pilot or Production
- Missing contract artifacts: restrict to contained usage until remediated
- No active owner: initiate retirement review within one review cycle
- In-scope and out-of-scope overlap: block promotion and return to the owner for contract revision
page_texts.31:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-001-ai-agent-definition.md#governance-oversight]

### Governance Oversight

- **Standards Owner**: Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board
- **Compliance Manager**: Platform Governance Team (monthly metadata currency checks)
- **Governance Body**: Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board (exception approvals and escalation)
- **Subject Matter Experts**: High-Tech role leads (quality gate reviews)
